name: THAILAND

lead: Thailand sits at the heart of Southeast Asia — ancient temples, misty mountains in the north, warm beaches in the south, and buzzing Bangkok in the middle. The only nation never colonised by Europeans, its name means Land of the Free. From Muay Thai gyms to floating markets, every corner pulses with colour, flavour, and smiles.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow!

geo: Thailand is shaped like a long axe. The wide top half is rugged highlands and river valleys draining into the Chao Phraya. The narrow southern strip — the Kra Peninsula — hangs between the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman Sea.

The north has mist-draped mountains including Doi Inthanon at 2,565 m. The south has thousands of islands, bright coral reefs, and limestone cliffs that shoot straight out of turquoise water like giant green teeth.
animals: Thailand's most famous animal is the Asian elephant — once used in battle and logging, now protected in national parks. Around 4,000–4,400 wild elephants roam forests like Khao Yai, and the rare white elephant is a sacred royal symbol.

The Siamese fighting fish — a jewel-bright freshwater fish — is the national aquatic animal, bred here for over 1,000 years. Clouded leopards, Indochinese tigers, and sun bears still prowl the dense northern forests.
culture: Thailand is deeply Buddhist — over 93% follow the faith, and the country has more than 40,000 temples. Young men often spend weeks as monks. The graceful Wai greeting, palms pressed together, means everything from hello to thank you.

Food is a national passion: fragrant curries, tangy papaya salad, and Pad Thai noodles. Songkran, the Thai New Year in April, is the world's biggest water fight — everyone gets soaked to wash away bad luck.
history: The first great Thai kingdoms rose at Sukhothai in the 13th century, followed by powerful Ayutthaya, which ruled for 400 years. Clever kings kept European colonial powers at bay, making Thailand the only Southeast Asian nation never colonised.
In 1939 the country renamed itself from Siam to Thailand — meaning Land of the Free. Bangkok's ceremonial name is 168 letters long, earning a Guinness World Record for the planet's longest city name.
wows: Bangkok's ceremonial full name is 168 letters long — a Guinness World Record.
The world's largest solid gold Buddha, 5.5 tonnes, hid under plaster in Bangkok for around 200 years.
Thailand has over 40,000 Buddhist temples — more than most countries have petrol stations.
Thailand is the only country in Southeast Asia never colonised by a European power.
Siamese fighting fish were first kept as pets in Thailand over 1,000 years ago.
Pad Thai noodles were invented in the 1940s by government order to cut wartime rice use.
Doi Inthanon was renamed for the last ruler of Chiang Mai, whose remains are buried near its summit.

myths.fact: Pad Thai was invented in the 1940s when the government promoted a noodle recipe to stretch rice supplies in WWII. Tasty, but thoroughly modern.
Wild Asian elephants are endangered — only around 4,000–4,400 survive in Thai forests. You are far more likely to see one at a sanctuary.
